definition_zh: 叶子；书页；薄片；（桌子的）活动板；翻（书）
definition_en: the flat green part of a plant; a sheet of paper or a thin sheet of metal; a hinged board that extends a table; to turn pages
core_image: 一片扁平的绿色薄片从茎上伸出，把阳光摊开接住
scene: 正午的强光直射下来，这片叶子慢慢调整角度，把光线错开。A single leaf turns toward the light.
sceneCN: 这里 leaf 指「植物进行光合的扁平器官」（第 1 个义项：植物的叶）；句意为一片叶子朝光转动。

senses.title: The flat green organ of a plant
senses.titleCN: 植物进行光合的扁平器官
senses.definition: the flat, usually green organ in which a plant captures light
senses.definitionCN: 植物捕获光能的扁平器官，通常为绿色
senses.example: A single leaf turns toward the light.
senses.exampleCN: 一片叶子朝光转动。
senses.why: Leaf comes from Old English leaf, a word for the blade of a plant, and the whole plant world is built on that one flat shape.
senses.whyCN: leaf 来自古英语，指植物的扁片；整个植物界都建立在这一个扁平形状上。

senses.title: A sheet in a book
senses.definition: one sheet of a book, with its two sides
senses.definitionCN: 书中一张纸，含正反两面
senses.example: She tore a leaf from the notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 她从笔记本上撕下一张纸。
senses.why: A page is thin, flat and turns over, so the plant word was borrowed for paper, and both still 'turn'.
senses.whyCN: 纸页薄、平、会翻，于是植物的词被借去指纸，两者至今都「翻」。

senses.title: A very thin sheet of metal
senses.definition: a thin sheet of metal, as gold leaf used in gilding
senses.definitionCN: 极薄的金属片，如贴金用的金箔
senses.example: The dome was finished with gold leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 穹顶最后贴上了金箔。
senses.why: Metal beaten thin enough to flutter behaves like a leaf, and crafts adopted the plant name.
senses.whyCN: 金属被打薄到能飘动，举止就像叶子，手艺行当于是采用了这个植物名。

senses.title: A hinged board on a table
senses.titleCN: 桌面上可翻起或抽出的板
senses.definition: a board hinged or sliding in a table to extend its top
senses.definitionCN: 桌面上铰接或滑动以加长桌面的板
senses.example: Pull out the leaf to seat six.
senses.exampleCN: 把活动板拉出来就能坐六个人。
senses.why: The board opens like a leaf unfolding, so furniture makers kept the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这块板打开时像叶子展开，家具匠于是沿用同一个词。

senses.title: Tea or tobacco leaf
senses.definition: the dried leaf of tea or tobacco as a product
senses.definitionCN: 作为产品的茶叶或烟叶
senses.example: The tea leaf is rolled before drying.
senses.exampleCN: 茶叶在烘干前要揉捻。
senses.why: Trade names the product by the organ harvested, so whole industries speak of leaf.
senses.whyCN: 行业按采收的器官给产品命名，于是整个行业都说「叶」。

senses.title: To turn pages quickly
senses.definition: to turn pages, especially quickly or casually
senses.definitionCN: 翻动书页，尤指快速地翻
senses.example: He leafed through the report before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前他把报告翻了一遍。
senses.why: The verb comes from the noun for a page: moving a page is moving a leaf.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自指纸页的名词：动一页就是动一片叶。

senses.title: To turn over a new leaf
senses.definition: to begin behaving better after a period of bad behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在不良行为之后开始好好做
senses.example: She turned over a new leaf after the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 受到警告后她改过自新。
senses.why: In an old book a leaf is a page, so turning one over means starting a fresh side of the record.
senses.whyCN: 在旧时的书里，leaf 就是一页，翻过去意味着从记录的另一面重新开始。

senses.title: A leaf-like part or scale
senses.titleCN: 植物体上叶状的部位或鳞片
senses.definition: a leaf-like structure or scale, as in a moss or a bulb
senses.definitionCN: 苔类或鳞茎上的叶状结构或鳞片
senses.example: Each bulb leaf stores food through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 每片鳞叶整个冬天都在贮藏养分。
senses.why: Botany extends the word to any flat lateral organ, because function follows form rather than strict identity.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个词扩展到任何扁平的侧生器官，因为功能跟着形状走，而不拘于严格同一性。

intro.en: Leaf is native English, from Old English leaf, from Germanic laub; a link to Latin folium is sometimes suggested but not established.
intro.cn: leaf 是英语本族词，来自古英语 leaf，再往前是日耳曼语的 laub；有人提出它与拉丁 folium 有联系，但未获证实。

items.en: Old English leaf meant 'leaf' and also 'sheet of paper', so the page sense is as old as the word in English.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指「叶」，也指「纸页」，可见纸页义在英语中与这个词一样古老。

items.en: The Germanic form laub is behind German Laub 'foliage' and English leaf; the family is well attested.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 laub 是德语 Laub「叶丛」与英语 leaf 的来源，这个词族有充分书证。

items.en: A pre-Germanic form such as leubh- 'leaf, peel' is sometimes given, but it is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 有时给出 leubh-「叶、剥皮」这类前日耳曼形式，但那是重构，不是有书证词。

items.en: Because a page is a leaf, English kept leaf for paper long after French page entered the language.
items.cn: 因为一页就是一片叶，法语 page 进入英语后，leaf 仍长期保留纸页义。

items.en: Gilders and cabinetmakers extended the word to thin metal and to hinged boards, both flat and leaf-like.
items.cn: 贴金匠与家具匠把它扩展到薄金属与铰接板，两者都扁而像叶。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the suggested link between Germanic laub and Latin folium is a hypothesis; no common ancestor has been demonstrated, so any such form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：日耳曼 laub 与拉丁 folium 的联系只是假说，尚未证明共同祖形，凡给出的此类形式都是重构。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that are unrelated in root from true relatives; group two holds leaf words by shape.
note.cn: 第一组区分词根无关的外形相近词与真正的同族词；第二组按形状列出各类「叶」。

entries.definition: From Old English laefan 'to allow, leave behind', a verb, not a plant word at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 laefan「准许、留下」，是动词，与植物无关。

entries.definition: From be- plus lief 'dear', from a root meaning 'to love'; only the ending looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 be- 加 lief「亲爱的」，词根意为「爱」，只有词尾相像。

entries.definition: Leaf plus the diminutive -let: a small leaf or a single sheet of printed matter.
entries.definitionCN: leaf 加小称后缀 -let：小叶，或单张印刷品。

entries.definition: From Old English hlaf 'bread'; the shape is similar, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 hlaf「面包」；形状相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: The leaf of a grass, long and narrow; leaf is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指禾草的叶，长而窄；leaf 是通称。

entries.definition: The leaf of a fern or palm, large and divided; it is a special case of a leaf.
entries.definitionCN: 指蕨或棕榈的叶，大而分裂，是叶的一种特例。

entries.definition: The narrow leaf of a pine or fir; again a shape-specific leaf.
entries.definitionCN: 指松杉的针状叶，同样是按形状特指的叶。

entries.definition: The leaves of a plant as one mass; leaf counts a single blade.
entries.definitionCN: 把一株植物的叶当作一团；leaf 数的是单片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the native root, the real compounds and the real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用本族词根、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: Old English leaf meant both 'leaf' and 'page', which is why a book has leaves.
normal.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指叶也指纸页，所以书有「叶」。

normal.en: The family: leafy, leaflet, leafless, leafed.
normal.cn: 同族：leafy、leaflet、leafless、leafed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fallen leaves, leaf through, gold leaf, leaf litter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：落叶、翻阅、金箔、落叶层。

normal.en: The idiom turn over a new leaf comes from turning to a fresh page.
normal.cn: 习语「翻过新的一页」来自翻到崭新的一页。

normal.en: The verb leafs, leafed, leafing is regular, unlike the noun plural leaves.
normal.cn: 动词 leafs、leafed、leafing 是规则的，与名词复数 leaves 不同。

abstract.en: Picture a table opening like a flower when the extra board slides out.
abstract.cn: 想象多出的板滑出时，桌子像花一样打开。

abstract.en: Picture a record with two sides, and you decide to start on the clean one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张两面都有记录的纸，你决定从干净的那面重新开始。

abstract.en: Picture a bulb as a stack of thick leaves waiting underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个鳞茎是地下叠着的一摞厚叶。

examples.en: A fallen leaf floated down the gutter.
examples.cn: 一片落叶顺排水沟漂下去。

examples.en: He leafed through the atlas while he waited.
examples.cn: 等的时候他翻着地图册。

examples.en: The frame is covered with gold leaf by hand.
examples.cn: 框子用手工贴上金箔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离（leaf）开的叶」——从枝上离开的薄片 → 叶子；书页

root: 古英语 leaf「叶、纸页」，来自日耳曼语 laub；与拉丁 folium 的联系仅为假说，未证明共同祖形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one shape, thin and flat: a plant organ, a page, a metal sheet, a table board, a traded product, and finally the acts of turning pages and starting afresh.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在同一个形状上——薄而平：植物器官、纸页、金属片、桌板、交易产品，最后是翻页与重新开始这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thin flat blade, made to catch light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄而平的叶，天生用来接住光。

branches.en: SHAPE FIRST: the plant organ and its leaf-like variants share the flat form.
branches.cn: 形状在先：植物器官与其叶状变体共享扁平形状。

branches.en: PAGE AND TURNING: a page is a leaf, so reading is leafing.
branches.cn: 纸页与翻动：一页就是一片叶，所以阅读就是翻叶。

branches.en: METAL: gold beaten thin behaves like a leaf.
branches.cn: 金属：金子打薄后举止像叶。

branches.en: FURNITURE: a board opens the way a leaf unfolds.
branches.cn: 家具：一块板像叶一样展开。

branches.en: PRODUCT AND IDIOM: harvested leaf becomes trade, and a turned page becomes a fresh start.
branches.cn: 产品与习语：采下的叶成为商品，翻过的一页成为新开始。

intro.en: Leaf is a native Germanic word, so it has no Latin affixes; its compounds are English through and through, and no Latin cognate can be relied on.
intro.cn: leaf 是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁词缀；它的复合词纯属英语，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English leaf and Germanic laub supply the root; -y, -let and -less are native or Romance suffixes used on it, and no Latin cognate is established.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 leaf 与日耳曼 laub 提供词根；-y、-let、-less 是加在其上的后缀，拉丁同族词未获证实。

items.example: The word is native, not borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是本族词，不是借词。

items.example: German Laub preserves the old form.
items.exampleCN: 德语 Laub 保留了古老形式。
它把 leaf 变成 leafy。

items.example: A leafy hedge screened the door.
It makes leaflet, a small leaf.

items.meaning: a small leaf; a printed sheet

items.example: It makes leafless, bare of leaves.
A leafed stem rooted in water.
items.exampleCN: 一根带叶的茎在水里生根。

definition_zh: 学习；学会；得知；记住
definition_en: to gain knowledge or skill by study or experience; to be told or find out information; to memorize
core_image: 一块海绵按进水里，把知识吸进来
scene: 开学第一周，新生每天抱着课本在图书馆坐到闭馆。Students learn new words by reading every day.
sceneCN: 这里 learn 是「通过学习获得知识」（第 1 个义项：学习）；句意为学生每天通过阅读学新词。

derivatives.zh: learn 加指人后缀 -er，指「学习者；初学者」
learn 加 -ing 名词化，指「学问；学习」
learn 加 -ed 构成形容词，指「博学的」（读作两音节）
加否定前缀 un-，指「忘掉已学的；矫正」

senses.title: To gain knowledge by study
senses.definition: to gain knowledge or skill by studying, practising or being taught
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习、练习或受教获得知识或技能
senses.example: Students learn new words by reading every day.
senses.exampleCN: 学生每天通过阅读学新词。
senses.why: The core image is absorbing: study pours information in the way a sponge takes up water.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「吸收」：学习像海绵吸水一样把信息灌进来。

senses.title: To memorize
senses.definition: to fix something in the memory so you can repeat it
senses.definitionCN: 把某事固定在记忆里以便能复述出来
senses.example: The actor learned all his lines in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 演员两天里背熟了全部台词。
senses.why: Memorizing is study turned inward: the knowledge is packed and stored, not just absorbed.
senses.whyCN: 记忆是把学习收进内部：知识被打包存起来，不只是吸收。

senses.title: To find out information
senses.definition: to be told or discover a fact, often news
senses.definitionCN: 被告知或发现某个事实，常指消息
senses.example: I learned of his illness only yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 我昨天才得知他生病的消息。
senses.why: Hearing news is also taking something in, so the same verb covers finding out.
senses.whyCN: 听到消息同样是接收东西，所以同一个动词也涵盖「得知」。

senses.title: To draw a lesson from experience
senses.definition: to change your behaviour because of what an experience taught you
senses.definitionCN: 因为经历给你的教训而改变行为
senses.example: She learned to check the weather before sailing.
senses.exampleCN: 她学会了出海前先看天气。
senses.why: Experience is a teacher: what it prints on you stays and guides later choices.
senses.whyCN: 经验是一位老师：它印在你身上的东西会留存并指引以后的选择。

senses.title: To teach (formal or old use)
senses.definition: to teach someone something (now rare, as in learn someone a thing)
senses.definitionCN: 教某人某事（今已罕见，如 learn someone a thing）
senses.example: An old ballad tells how the master learned the boy the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 一首老民谣讲师傅如何教男孩手艺。
senses.why: In older English the direction was reversed; modern English keeps this only in dialect.
senses.whyCN: 旧英语里方向是反过来的；现代英语只在方言里保留这种用法。

senses.title: To come to know a skill gradually
senses.definition: to reach the point where you can do something well after practice
senses.definitionCN: 经过练习达到能把某事做好的程度
senses.example: He is still learning to drive.
senses.exampleCN: 他还在学开车。
senses.why: Skill grows by repeated absorption and correction, which the verb pictures as an ongoing process.
senses.whyCN: 技能靠反复吸收与纠正而增长，动词把它画成一个进行中的过程。

senses.title: To learn the hard way
senses.definition: to discover something by suffering the consequences yourself
senses.definitionCN: 亲自承受后果后才明白某事
senses.example: I learned the hard way that cheap tools break.
senses.exampleCN: 我是吃了亏才知道便宜工具会坏。
senses.why: The image is knowledge bought with pain: the lesson is absorbed because the cost was real.
senses.whyCN: 意象是用痛苦买来的知识：因为代价真实，教训才被真正吸收。

intro.en: Learn comes from Old English leornian "to get knowledge", of uncertain wider origin; it replaced older native words and has stayed central to English.
intro.cn: learn 来自古英语 leornian「获得知识」，更早来源不确定；它取代了更老的本族词，一直居于英语核心。

items.en: Old English leornian meant 'to acquire knowledge', possibly with an idea of treading a track, following a path of study.
items.cn: 古英语 leornian 意为「获得知识」，可能含「踩着路径走、沿治学之路前行」的意思。

items.en: Related forms appear in other Germanic languages, but the exact root beyond Germanic is not agreed on.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语言里有相关形式，但日耳曼语之外的词根尚无定论。

items.en: In Middle English the word widened to cover both teaching and learning, a direction it later lost.
items.cn: 中古英语里这个词兼指教与学，后来这个方向用法消失了。

items.en: Modern English keeps learn for acquiring knowledge, learning and finding out, and leaves teaching to teach.
items.cn: 现代英语让 learn 专指获得知识、学会与得知，把「教」交给了 teach。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Germanic origin of leornian is disputed; suggestions exist but none is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：leornian 在日耳曼语之前的来源有争议，有若干猜测但无一被证实。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes and true relatives; group two collects verbs about taking in knowledge or news.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近词与真正的同族词；第二组收集关于接收知识或消息的动词。

entries.definition: From Old English hleonian "to lean"; only the spelling after l-e-a is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 hleonian「倚靠」；只共享 l-e-a 之后的拼写。

entries.definition: From Old English earnian "to earn"; one letter shorter, no kinship with learn.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 earnian「赚取」；少一个字母，与 learn 无亲缘。

entries.definition: Learn plus the agent suffix -er: someone who is learning.
entries.definitionCN: learn 加施事后缀 -er：正在学习的人。

entries.definition: The noun for knowledge gained by study, also scholarship in general.
entries.definitionCN: 由学习获得知识的名词，也泛指学问。

entries.definition: To apply the mind deliberately to a subject; learn stresses the result.
entries.definitionCN: 有意识地钻研一个科目；learn 强调结果。

entries.definition: To come to have knowledge or skill, often by effort over time.
entries.definitionCN: 经过长期努力获得知识或技能。

entries.definition: To discover a fact, often by asking or investigating; learn covers the moment you are told.
entries.definitionCN: （通过询问或调查）发现事实；learn 涵盖「被告知」的那一刻。

entries.definition: To learn something so well that you control it fully.
entries.definitionCN: 学到能完全驾驭的程度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real word family, collocations and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词族、搭配与习语。

normal.en: Old English leornian meant 'to get knowledge'; the word has kept that job for a thousand years.
normal.cn: 古英语 leornian 意为「获得知识」，这个词一千年来没换过工作。

normal.en: The family: learner, learning, learned (scholarly), unlearn.
normal.cn: 词族：learner、learning、learned（博学的）、unlearn。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: learn from, learn by heart, learn a lesson, learn the ropes.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：向……学习、背熟、吸取教训、学会门道。

normal.en: Two past forms: learned and learnt, both correct in British English.
normal.cn: 两种过去式：learned 与 learnt，英式英语里都对。

normal.en: The adjective learned has two syllables, unlike the verb form learned.
normal.cn: 形容词 learned 读两个音节，与动词形式不同。

abstract.en: Picture your head as a jar filling drop by drop each time you read.
abstract.cn: 想象脑袋像罐子，每次阅读都滴进一滴水。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson printed on your palm after you touch a hot stove.
abstract.cn: 想象碰了热炉子后，教训印在手掌上。

abstract.en: Picture news arriving as a letter you open and read in one second.
abstract.cn: 想象消息像一封信，一秒打开读完，你就「得知」了。

examples.en: Children learn languages far faster than adults.
examples.cn: 儿童学语言比成人快得多。

examples.en: We only learned the truth after the meeting ended.
examples.cn: 会议结束后我们才得知真相。

examples.en: Every mistake teaches you something, if you are willing to learn.
examples.cn: 只要你愿意学，每个错误都能教你一点东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「勒恩」——勒住懒惰、恩赐知识 → 学习；学会

root: 古英语 leornian「获得知识」，词根在日耳曼语之前的来源不确定；有人联想「循路而行」的意象，仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all grow from one motion: something is taken in — knowledge by study, facts by news, lessons by pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都从同一个动作长出：有东西被吸收——靠学习得知识，靠消息得知情，靠痛苦得教训。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vessel filling as knowledge is poured in.
core.cn: 核心意象：知识灌入时容器逐渐装满。

branches.en: ABSORBING BY STUDY: knowledge enters through reading and practice, gradually building skill.
branches.cn: 靠学习吸收：知识经由阅读与练习进入，逐渐练成本领。

branches.en: PACKING IN: study turned inward becomes memorizing.
branches.cn: 向内打包：学习收进内部就成了背诵。

branches.en: NEWS ARRIVES: the same intake covers finding out facts.
branches.cn: 消息到达：同一种接收也涵盖得知事实。

branches.en: PAID LESSONS: experience teaches, sometimes at a cost.
branches.cn: 付费的课：经验也会教人，有时要付代价。

branches.en: REVERSED FLOW: in old usage the teacher also "learned" the pupil.
branches.cn: 倒流：旧用法里老师也「learn」学生。

intro.en: Learn is a native English verb with no Latin prefix; its family is built with small native suffixes.
intro.cn: learn 是本族英语动词，没有拉丁前缀；词族靠小的本族后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established for learn, so the Latin section stays empty; the items list native suffix work.
latinIntro.cn: learn 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目列出本族后缀的加工。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语本族的。
它把 learn 变成 learner。

items.example: A slow learner needs more time.
items.exampleCN: 学得慢的人需要更多时间。
它把 learn 变成 learning。
古老的学问装满了图书馆。
博学的法官引用拉丁文。
它把 learn 变成 unlearn。

items.example: It makes learnable, easy to learn.

definition_zh: 离开；留下；把……留给；请假；许可
definition_en: to go away from a place; to let something stay or remain; to cause something to stay behind; permission to be absent
core_image: 转身走出门口，身后留下的东西还在原处
scene: 最后一班地铁进站，他收起行李往闸机走去。Please leave your umbrella outside the room.
sceneCN: 这里 leave 是「使某物留在某处」（第 3 个义项：留下某物）；句意为请把伞留在门外。

derivatives.zh: leave 加副词化后缀构成复合词，指「剩饭剩菜；剩余物」
来自同族词 depart（de- + partir），指「离开；出发」
leave 加施事后缀 -er，指「离开者；离职者」

senses.title: To go away from a place
senses.definition: to depart from a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地或某人
senses.example: The train leaves at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 火车八点开出。
senses.why: Going away is the picture of turning your back and moving out of range.
senses.whyCN: 「离开」就是转过身、走出范围的那幅画面。

senses.title: To let something stay
senses.definition: to allow something to remain where it is
senses.definitionCN: 允许某物留在原处
senses.example: Leave the door open, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请让门开着。
senses.why: What you do not carry away stays behind, so not-taking is a kind of leaving.
senses.whyCN: 你没带走的东西就留在原地，所以「不带走」也是一种 leave。

senses.title: To put something somewhere deliberately
senses.definition: to place something so that it stays there for someone or some purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某目的把某物放在那里
senses.example: I left a note on your desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我在你桌上留了张字条。
senses.why: Placing is leaving with intent: the thing is meant to wait where it is.
senses.whyCN: 放置是带意图的留下：那东西就是要在原地等着。

senses.title: To cause a state or result
senses.definition: to make something be in a particular state after an action
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在动作之后处于特定状态
senses.example: The storm left the streets covered in leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后街道上盖满落叶。
senses.why: The actor walks away but the effect stays, so the result is what he left.
senses.whyCN: 施动者走了，效果却留下，所以结果就是他留下的东西。

senses.title: To give by will or transfer
senses.definition: to give property or responsibility to someone after death or on departure
senses.definitionCN: 死后或离开时把财产或责任交给某人
senses.example: She left the house to her daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把房子留给女儿。
senses.why: Departure from life or a job passes things to those who stay.
senses.whyCN: 从生命或职位离开时，东西就传给留下的人。

senses.title: Permission; time off
senses.definition: official permission to be absent, or the period of absence itself
senses.definitionCN: 获准缺席的正式许可，或缺席的那段时间
senses.example: He is on sick leave this week.
senses.exampleCN: 他本周休病假。
senses.why: Being away needs approval, so the word names both the permission and the absence itself.
senses.whyCN: 离开需要批准，所以这个词既指许可也指缺席期本身。

senses.title: To stop doing something
senses.definition: to stop doing or dealing with something
senses.definitionCN: 停止做或不再处理某事
senses.example: Leave the arguing and start the work.
senses.exampleCN: 别吵了，开始干活吧。
senses.why: Walking away from an activity is leaving it behind like a place.
senses.whyCN: 从一件事上抽身，就像离开一个地方。

senses.title: To depend on someone else
senses.definition: to let another person decide or handle something
senses.definitionCN: 让别人决定或处理某事
senses.example: Leave it to me.
senses.exampleCN: 交给我吧。
senses.why: You walk away from the decision and it waits in the hands of whoever stays.
senses.whyCN: 你从决定旁边走开，它就留在留下的人手里。

intro.en: Leave comes from Old English laefan "to allow, leave behind", from Germanic laibjan, related to a root meaning "to remain".
intro.cn: leave 来自古英语 laefan「准许、留下」，出自日耳曼语 laibjan，与意为「留存」的词根相关。

items.en: Old English laefan meant 'to leave, allow, bequeath', already covering both going away and letting stay.
items.cn: 古英语 laefan 意为「离开、准许、遗赠」，已同时涵盖离去与留存两方向。

items.en: Germanic laibjan is behind the English verb and related to German bleiben 'to remain', from a root meaning 'to stick, stay'.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 laibjan 是英语动词的来源，并与德语 bleiben「停留」同源，词根意为「粘住、留下」。

items.en: Norse influence may have strengthened the sense of permission and departure in northern English.
items.cn: 北欧语的影响可能强化了英格兰北部用法中「许可」与「离去」的义项。

items.en: In Middle English leave developed the noun sense of permission, then of authorized absence.
items.cn: 中古英语里 leave 发展出「许可」的名词义，进而指获批的缺席。

items.en: Modern English kept both directions: go away, let stay, and added the workplace holiday sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留双向用法：离去、任其留下，并新增了职场休假义。

note.en: Group one flags words that only look alike; group two collects words of going away and staying.
note.cn: 第一组标出仅外形相近的词；第二组收集「离去」与「留存」的词。

entries.definition: The plant word; ends in -f not -ve and belongs to Germanic laub.
entries.definitionCN: 植物词；词尾是 -f 不是 -ve，属于日耳曼语 laub 词族。

entries.definition: From Old English libban "to live"; only the letters after l-i look close.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 libban「活着」；只是 l-i 之后的字母相像。

entries.definition: Someone who leaves, as in school leavers.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的人，如 school leaver（离校生）。

entries.definition: What is left over after the rest is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 其余部分走后剩下的东西。

entries.definition: To go away, especially on a journey; leave is the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 离去，尤指启程；leave 是日常用词。

entries.definition: To stop or resign; it stresses ending an activity or job.
entries.definitionCN: 停止或辞职；强调终结某项活动或工作。

entries.definition: To leave something completely and finally, often without care.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底且最终地抛下，常含不顾不管。

entries.definition: To stay where you are; the staying side of the same picture.
entries.definitionCN: 留在原地；同一画面的「留下」一侧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real family and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Old English laefan meant 'leave behind, allow', so both directions are ancient.
normal.cn: 古英语 laefan 意为「留下、准许」，两个方向都很古老。

normal.en: German bleiben "to remain" is a cousin from the same root.
normal.cn: 德语 bleiben「停留」是同一词根的表亲。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: leave for, leave behind, leave out, take French leave.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：动身前往、留下、遗漏、不告而别。

normal.en: The past form left also works as an adjective, as in the left side.
normal.cn: 过去式 left 还能作形容词，如「左边」。

normal.en: On leave means officially away: sick leave, annual leave, maternity leave.
normal.cn: on leave 指获批离岗：病假、年假、产假。

abstract.en: Picture your footprints behind you on wet sand as you walk off.
abstract.cn: 想象你走开后，湿沙上留下一串脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a note under a magnet on the fridge, waiting for someone.
abstract.cn: 想象冰箱磁铁下压着一张字条，等人来取。

abstract.en: Picture a will passing keys to the one who stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸遗嘱把钥匙交给留下的人。

examples.en: We leave for Shanghai early tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 我们明早动身去上海。

examples.en: The night shift left the tools exactly where they found them.
examples.cn: 夜班把工具原样留在原地。

examples.en: She took two weeks of leave after the project ended.
examples.cn: 项目结束后她休了两周假。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离吾」——离吾而去 → 离开；留下

root: 古英语 laefan「留下、准许」，出自日耳曼语 laibjan，与「留存」义词根相关；与德语 bleiben 同源是学界共识。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split along two arrows: going away yourself, or letting things stay behind when you go.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿两支箭头展开：自己走开，或走开时让东西留在后面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway; you step through and things stay on the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门；你跨过去，东西留在另一边。

branches.en: WALKING OFF: from places and from activities alike.
branches.cn: 走开：既离开地方，也抽离活动。

branches.en: THINGS THAT WAIT: letting stay, or placing on purpose.
branches.cn: 等待之物：任其留下，或有意放置。

branches.en: THE AFTER-EFFECT: results left hanging in the air.
branches.cn: 后续效果：留在空气里的结果。

branches.en: PASSING ON: property and duties go to those who stay.
branches.cn: 传递：财产与职责交给留下的人。

branches.en: OFFICIAL AWAY: permission, holiday, and handing decisions to others.
branches.cn: 获批离场：许可、假期，以及把决定交给别人。

intro.en: Leave is a native Germanic verb with no Latin prefix; its family is small and built with native suffixes.
intro.cn: leave 是日耳曼本族动词，没有拉丁前缀；词族不大，用本族后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native word-building.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族构词。

items.example: The verb is native to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语本族的。
它把 leave 变成 leaver。
它与 leave 合成 leftover。
冰箱里塞满冷掉的剩菜。

items.example: Three apples were left on the plate.

items.exampleCN: 德语 bleiben 保留了形式。

definition_zh: 左边的；剩下的（leave 的过去式和过去分词）
definition_en: the side that is opposite the right when facing forward; the past form of leave; remaining
core_image: 面向前方时，心脏偏向的那一侧
scene: 路边停车后他伸手去拉左侧的车门。Turn left at the second crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 left 是「方向上的左」（第 1 个义项：左边的）；句意为在第二个路口向左转。

pos.zh: leave 的过去式/过去分词：离开；留下

derivatives.zh: left 加 hand 加 -ed，指「惯用左手的」
left 与 over 合成，指「剩余的」

senses.title: The left side or direction
senses.definition: the side opposite the right when a person faces forward
senses.definitionCN: 人面向前方时与右相对的一侧
senses.example: Turn left at the second crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二个路口向左转。
senses.why: Facing forward fixes two sides, and left names the heart-side one.
senses.whyCN: 面向前方定了两侧，left 指心脏所在的一侧。

senses.title: Political left
senses.definition: groups favouring social change and collective welfare
senses.definitionCN: 主张社会变革与集体福利的派别
senses.example: The left pushed for the new labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 左派推动通过了新劳动法。
senses.why: Meeting rooms once placed radicals on the left of the chair, and the seat became the label.
senses.whyCN: 旧时会议厅里激进派坐在议长左侧，座位就成了标签。

senses.title: Remaining
senses.definition: what still exists after the rest is gone or used
senses.definitionCN: 其余部分消失或用完之后还存在的东西
senses.example: There is nothing left in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 锅里什么都不剩了。
senses.why: What leave leaves behind is left: the past participle hardened into a word of its own.
senses.whyCN: leave 留下的东西就是 left：过去分词固化成了独立的词。

senses.title: Past form of leave
senses.definition: the past tense and participle of the verb leave
senses.definitionCN: 动词 leave 的过去式与过去分词
senses.example: He left the office at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他中午离开了办公室。
senses.why: Grammar gives left a second life as a verb form, separate from the direction word.
senses.whyCN: 语法让 left 以动词形式获得第二生命，与方向词分开。

senses.title: A left-hand blow (sport)
senses.definition: in boxing, a punch delivered with the left hand or fist
senses.definitionCN: 拳击中用左手或左拳打出的击打
senses.example: He ended the round with a sharp left.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记凌厉的左拳结束了回合。
senses.why: The side word names the tool used, so the punch borrows the direction.
senses.whyCN: 侧位词命名了使用的工具，于是这一拳借用了方向名。

senses.title: Left-hand side of a page or stage
senses.definition: the left side of an open page, or the stage side from the audience view
senses.definitionCN: 翻开书页的左侧，或观众视角下舞台的左侧
senses.example: The notes sit in the left margin.
senses.exampleCN: 批注在左边的页边。
senses.why: Books and stages keep a fixed geometry, so the side word marks positions on them.
senses.whyCN: 书籍与舞台几何固定，方向词就标出上面的位置。

intro.en: Two words share the spelling left. The direction word comes from Old English left "weak, foolish" (the left hand was the unskilled hand); the verb form is the past of leave.
intro.cn: 两个词共用拼写 left。方向词来自古英语 left「虚弱的、笨拙的」（左手曾是笨拙之手）；动词形式是 leave 的过去式。

items.en: Old English left meant 'weak'; the left hand was thought the clumsy hand, so the side took the name.
items.cn: 古英语 left 意为「虚弱」；左手被视为笨拙之手，这一侧便得了这个名。

items.en: The word is native Germanic; related forms appear as lyft with a sense of 'weak, idle' in northern usage.
items.cn: 该词是日耳曼本族词；北方用法中相关形式 lyft 带「虚弱、闲散」义。

items.en: Middle English fixed left as the standard side word, pushing out older sinistral terms.
items.cn: 中古英语把 left 固定为标准方位词，取代了更老的 sinistral 一类说法。

items.en: Modern English added the political sense from seating customs in assemblies.
items.cn: 现代英语因议会座席习俗新增了政治义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link of the weak-hand word to other Germanic roots is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：「虚弱之手」一词与其他日耳曼词根的联系仍有争议。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects direction and remainder words.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近词；第二组收集方向与剩余之词。

entries.definition: To raise or a ride in a car; one letter apart from left, no kinship.
entries.definitionCN: 举起或搭便车；与 left 仅差一字母，无亲缘。

entries.definition: Built from left (past of leave) plus over.
entries.definitionCN: 由 left（leave 的过去式）加 over 构成。

entries.definition: A flat floating platform; only the consonant frame looks close.
entries.definitionCN: 平底漂浮物；只有辅音框架相像。

entries.definition: The other side, also a word for correct.
entries.definitionCN: 另一侧，也表「正确」。

entries.definition: Latin for the left side, later tinted with evil.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语的「左侧」，后染上凶意。

entries.definition: Still present after others are gone; matches the participle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 其余消失后仍在；对应过去分词义。

entries.definition: French for left, meaning socially awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 法语的「左」，转指社交笨拙。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real spellings, seats and phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拼写、座席与短语。

normal.en: Old English left meant 'weak'; the left hand was the clumsy one.
normal.cn: 古英语 left 意为「虚弱」，左手曾是笨拙之手。

normal.en: Turn left, on the left, the left wing are the common phrases.
normal.cn: turn left、on the left、the left wing 是常用短语。

normal.en: Nothing left comes from the past participle of leave.
normal.cn: nothing left 来自 leave 的过去分词。

normal.en: In politics the left and the right came from where members sat.
normal.cn: 政治上的左派右派来自议员的座位。

normal.en: A left in boxing is a left-hand punch.
normal.cn: 拳击里的 left 是左手拳。

abstract.en: Picture your heart leaning to one side when you face north.
abstract.cn: 想象面向北方时心脏偏向一侧。

abstract.en: Picture an empty pot scraped clean, nothing left.
abstract.cn: 想象一口锅被刮得干干净净，什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture the assembly hall with reformers seated on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象议会大厅里改革者坐在一侧。

examples.en: The bank is on your left as you come out of the station.
examples.cn: 出车站后银行就在你左手边。

examples.en: Only ten minutes were left before the deadline.
examples.cn: 离截止只剩十分钟。

examples.en: She writes with her left hand.
examples.cn: 她用左手写字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离夫特」——离开后剩下的一侧 → 左边；剩下的

root: 方向词 left 来自古英语 left「虚弱」（左手为笨拙之手）；动词 left 是 leave 的过去式，两者拼写偶合。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses follow two separate histories: a side word that grew political, and a verb form that turned into a word for remainder.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项沿两条独立历史：一个方位词长出政治义，一个动词形式长出「剩余」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the side where the heart sits; and what stays behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：心脏所在的一侧；以及身后剩下的东西。

branches.en: THE SIDE: direction, pages, stages, and the fist that uses it.
branches.cn: 侧位：方向、书页、舞台，以及用到这只手的一拳。

branches.en: THE SEAT: assembly seating turned a side into a movement.
branches.cn: 座席：会议座位把方位变成了派别。

branches.en: WHAT STAYS: the participle hardened into remainder.
branches.cn: 留存之物：过去分词固化成「剩余」。

branches.en: THE VERB FORM: left as the past of leave.
branches.cn: 动词形式：left 作 leave 的过去式。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: facing forward fixes the two sides forever.
branches.cn: 几何：面向前方，两侧永远确定。

intro.en: Left is a short native word with no affixes of its own; compounds and derivatives are formed by attaching English elements.
intro.cn: left 是无词缀的短小本族词；复合词与派生词靠附加英语成分构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established, so the Latin section stays empty; the items list native compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目列出本族复合词。

items.exampleCN: 一位左撇子击球手上场。

items.example: The leftist wrote for the paper.
items.exampleCN: 那位左派人士为报社撰稿。

items.example: The left wing backed the reform.

items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了更阴暗的色彩。
法语有相同的色彩引申。

definition_zh: 腿；腿脚；（桌椅的）腿；一段行程
definition_en: the limb of a person or animal used for standing and walking; a support of a table or chair; one part of a journey or competition
core_image: 从躯干伸出的长条支撑，走路全靠它
scene: 马拉松到了半程，他的双腿开始发沉。The last leg of the relay was the hardest.
sceneCN: 这里 leg 是「行程的一段」（第 4 个义项：赛程或旅程的一段）；句意为接力最后一棒最难。

pos.zh: 腿；（家具）腿；（旅程/竞赛的）一段

derivatives.zh: leg 加 -ed，指「有……条腿的」（如 long-legged）
leg 与 work 合成，指「跑腿工作」

senses.title: The limb for standing and walking
senses.definition: the limb from hip to foot used for standing and walking
senses.definitionCN: 从髋到脚、用于站立与行走的肢体
senses.example: He stretched his legs under the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把腿伸直放在桌子下面。
senses.why: The body\u2019s pillars carry the whole frame, which is the plain picture.
senses.whyCN: 身体的柱子撑起整个架子，这就是最直观的画面。

senses.title: A support of furniture
senses.definition: one of the upright supports of a table or chair
senses.definitionCN: 桌椅等直立支撑件之一
senses.example: One leg of the chair is loose.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子有一条腿松了。
senses.why: Furniture stands the way bodies stand, so the limb lent its name to the support.
senses.whyCN: 家具站立的姿态像身体，肢体便把名字借给了支撑件。

senses.title: A stage of a competition
senses.titleCN: 竞赛的一段（如接力棒次）
senses.definition: one part of a race or contest run in stages
senses.definitionCN: 分阶段进行的比赛的一部分
senses.example: The team won the first leg of the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 该队赢下了杯赛首回合。
senses.why: A contest cut into pieces has legs like a journey, each piece one push.
senses.whyCN: 切成片段的比赛像旅程一样有「腿」，每段是一程冲刺。

senses.title: A part of a journey
senses.definition: one section of a journey between stops
senses.definitionCN: 行程中两站之间的一段
senses.example: The last leg of the relay was the hardest.
senses.exampleCN: 接力最后一棒最难。
senses.why: A route is walked piece by piece, and each piece is one leg of it.
senses.whyCN: 路线是一段段走完的，每一段就是一 leg。

senses.title: To go on foot (informal)
senses.definition: to walk or run somewhere, used in phrases like leg it
senses.definitionCN: 步行或跑去某处，用于 leg it 等短语
senses.example: We legged it to the station in five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 我们五分钟一路狂奔到了车站。
senses.why: When vehicles fail, the limbs take over, so the verb points at bare walking.
senses.whyCN: 车靠不住时就得靠腿，动词于是直指用脚走。

senses.title: The long thin part of clothing
senses.definition: the part of trousers that covers a leg
senses.definitionCN: 裤子上覆盖腿的部分
senses.example: The tear is on the left leg.
senses.exampleCN: 破口在左裤腿。
senses.why: The cloth follows the limb it covers, so trousers have legs too.
senses.whyCN: 布料跟随它包裹的肢体，裤子也就有了「腿」。

senses.title: A wine\u2019s streaks on glass
senses.definition: the streaks wine leaves on the side of a glass
senses.definitionCN: 酒液在杯壁留下的纹路
senses.example: The wine shows fine legs.
senses.exampleCN: 这酒挂杯细密。
senses.why: Liquid runs down slowly like a thin limb, and tasters named the streaks.
senses.whyCN: 液体像细肢一样缓缓流下，品鉴者便给纹路起了这个名字。

intro.en: Leg comes from Old Norse leggr "leg, bone of the leg", replacing older native English words; its pre-Norse trail is not fully clear.
intro.cn: leg 来自古诺斯语 leggr「腿、腿骨」，取代了更老的本族词；诺斯语之前的轨迹不完全清楚。

items.en: Old Norse leggr meant 'leg' or 'leg-bone', and settlers brought the word into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 leggr 意为「腿」或「腿骨」，定居者把这个词带进了英格兰北部。

items.en: Middle English spread leg widely and it pushed out older words for the limb.
items.cn: 中古英语里 leg 广泛传播，取代了更老的肢体词。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): whether leggr connects to a root meaning 'to bend at the joint' is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：leggr 是否与「关节弯折」义词根相关仍有争议。

items.en: Modern English extended leg to furniture, journeys, contests and even wine glasses.
items.cn: 现代英语把 leg 扩展到家具、旅程、比赛乃至酒杯。

items.en: It sits inside the Germanic word stock of the north, alongside other Norse body words.
items.cn: 它属于北方日耳曼词汇库，与其他诺斯语身体词并列。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes without kinship; group two lists limb and stretch words.
note.cn: 第一组标出无亲缘的形近词；第二组列出肢体与延伸之词。

entries.definition: To fall behind; one vowel apart, a different Germanic word.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；仅差一个元音，是另一个日耳曼词。

entries.definition: Past of lead; same sound, unrelated history.
entries.definitionCN: lead 的过去式；同音但历史无关。

entries.definition: A close-fitting cover for the legs.
entries.definitionCN: 紧包腿部的衣着。

entries.definition: A formal word for an arm or leg; leg is the everyday one.
entries.definitionCN: 臂或腿的正式说法；leg 是日常用词。

entries.definition: The upper part of the leg only.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指腿的上段。

entries.definition: The part of the leg between knee and ankle.
entries.definitionCN: 膝与踝之间的部分。

entries.definition: One section of a journey; leg is more physical and sporting.
entries.definitionCN: 旅程的一段；leg 更偏身体与体育。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Norse root, the family and the idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用诺斯词根、词族与习语。

normal.en: Old Norse leggr meant leg or leg-bone; English borrowed it from the settlers.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 leggr 意为腿或腿骨，英语从定居者那里借来。

normal.en: Family: legged, legless, legwork, leggings.
normal.cn: 词族：legged、legless、legwork、leggings。

normal.en: Idioms: pull my leg, break a leg, on your last legs.
normal.cn: 习语：开玩笑、祝演出成功、快撑不住了。

normal.en: Furniture legs, journey legs and race legs all extend the limb.
normal.cn: 家具腿、旅程段、赛程段都延伸了「腿」。

normal.en: Break a leg wishes luck, never bad luck, in theatre talk.
normal.cn: 剧场用语里 break a leg 是祝好运，绝非坏话。

abstract.en: Picture a table wobbling because one leg is shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象一条桌腿偏短，桌子晃个不停。

abstract.en: Picture a map cut into walking pieces, one piece per day.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被切成一天一段的步行碎片。

abstract.en: Picture wine crawling down the glass like thin legs.
abstract.cn: 想象酒液像细腿一样沿杯壁爬下。

examples.en: After the match both legs ached for two days.
examples.cn: 赛后两条腿酸痛了两天。

examples.en: The final leg of the flight goes via Dubai.
examples.cn: 航程最后一段经迪拜中转。

examples.en: Stop pulling my leg and tell me the truth.
examples.cn: 别逗我了，说实话吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来个」——走路先来个抬腿 → 腿

root: 古诺斯语 leggr「腿、腿骨」，随北欧定居者进入英语；更早词根存疑，与「关节弯折」相关的说法仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all hang on one long prop: the body\u2019s pillar, then supports, route pieces, race pieces, cloth, and streaks in a glass.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都挂在一根长支撑上：身体的柱子，继而是家具支撑、路程段、赛程段、裤腿与挂杯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long prop that carries weight and moves you forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：承重并带你前进的长支撑。

branches.en: THE BODY\u2019S PILLAR: standing, walking, and legging it.
branches.cn: 身体的柱子：站立、行走与拔腿就跑。

branches.en: WHAT STANDS OR COVERS: furniture legs and trouser legs.
branches.cn: 站立或覆盖之物：家具腿与裤腿。

branches.en: PIECES OF A WAY: contest rounds and journey sections.
branches.cn: 路程的碎片：比赛回合与旅程段落。

branches.en: THIN LINES RUNNING: wine streaks named for the shape.
branches.cn: 细线流淌：挂杯因形得名。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: all extensions keep the idea of weight-bearing.
branches.cn: 轴心：一切引申都保留「承重」这一核心。

intro.en: Leg is a one-syllable Norse loan with no prefixes; its family is built by adding native suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: leg 是单音节诺斯借词，无前缀；词族靠本族后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native word-building.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族构词。

items.example: The loan came with the settlers.

items.exampleCN: 它把 leg 变成 legless。

items.example: A legless lizard looks like a snake.
Wool leggings kept out the wind.
We legged it home in the rain.
A friend gave him a leg up.

definition_zh: 柠檬；柠檬树；柠檬味；无用的东西（尤指有缺陷的汽车）
definition_en: a yellow citrus fruit with sour juice; the tree that bears it; its flavour; something that proves defective, especially a car
core_image: 黄皮酸果，一口把人酸得眯起眼
scene: 夏日午后，她切了两片黄果放进冰水。Fresh lemon makes the tea taste brighter.
sceneCN: 这里 lemon 是「水果」（第 1 个义项：柠檬果）；句意为鲜柠檬让茶喝起来更清爽。

derivatives.zh: lemon 加 -y，指「柠檬味的；柠檬色的」
lemon 加 -ade 饮料后缀，指「柠檬水」

senses.title: The sour yellow fruit
senses.definition: a yellow oval citrus fruit with very sour juice
senses.definitionCN: 黄色椭圆的柑橘类水果，汁极酸
senses.example: She squeezed half a lemon over the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她在鱼上挤了半个柠檬的汁。
senses.why: The fruit itself is the root picture: yellow skin, sharp juice, unmistakable smell.
senses.whyCN: 果实本身就是根意象：黄皮、酸汁、 unmistakable 的气味。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: the evergreen tree that produces lemons
senses.definitionCN: 长柠檬的常绿树
senses.example: Their garden has two lemon trees.
senses.exampleCN: 他们园里有两棵柠檬树。
senses.why: The fruit names the plant that carries it, as English often does.
senses.whyCN: 果名为树命名，这是英语的常态。

senses.title: The flavour or colour
senses.definition: the sharp flavour of lemon, or its pale yellow colour
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬的酸香风味，或其淡黄色
senses.example: The cake has a lemon flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个蛋糕有柠檬味。
senses.why: The fruit is so distinct that taste and colour borrow its name.
senses.whyCN: 果实特征鲜明，味与色都借它的名字。

senses.title: A defective product
senses.definition: something bought that turns out faulty, especially a car
senses.definitionCN: 买来后发现有问题之物，尤指汽车
senses.example: That used car turned out to be a lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆二手车结果是辆次品车。
senses.why: A sour fruit stands for a sour deal: sweet promises, bitter outcome.
senses.whyCN: 酸果代表酸涩的交易：承诺甜，结果苦。

senses.title: A silly or disappointing person
senses.titleCN: 傻里傻气或令人失望的人
senses.definition: a person who behaves foolishly or is a disappointment
senses.definitionCN: 行为傻气或让人失望的人
senses.example: Don\u2019t be such a lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯傻了。
senses.why: Calling a person a lemon keeps the sour, useless shade of the fruit.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作 lemon，保留了果实酸涩无用的色彩。

senses.title: A drink made with lemon
senses.definition: a drink flavoured or mixed with lemon juice
senses.definitionCN: 用柠檬汁调味或调制的饮品
senses.example: Two iced lemons, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请来两杯冰柠檬饮。
senses.why: Products take the name of the fruit that defines them.
senses.whyCN: 产品以定义它的水果为名。

intro.en: Lemon came into English through Old French and Medieval Latin limon, likely from Arabic laymun, which itself came from Persian.
intro.cn: lemon 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语 limon 进入英语，可能源自阿拉伯语 laymun，而后者又来自波斯语。

items.en: Persian limun is the likely starting point, naming the citrus fruit long traded in Asia.
items.cn: 波斯语 limun 很可能是起点，命名了亚洲长期贸易的柑橘果。

items.en: Arabic laymun carried the fruit and the word westward with trade.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 laymun 带着果实与词语随贸易西行。

items.en: Medieval Latin limon appears in European texts, keeping the trade route visible.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 limon 见于欧洲文献，贸易路线依稀可见。

items.en: Old French lemon brought the word across the Channel in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中古晚期，古法语 lemon 把词渡过了海峡。

items.en: Modern English kept lemon for the fruit and later coined the defective-product sense in American slang.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lemon 指果实，后来美国俚语又造出「次品」义。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects sour and citrus words.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集酸味与柑橘之词。

entries.definition: Lemon plus the drink suffix -ade.
entries.definitionCN: lemon 加饮品后缀 -ade。

entries.definition: A sweet gourd fruit; shares letters but the root is separate.
entries.definitionCN: 甜瓜；字母相叠，词根不同。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: The green citrus, sharper and smaller than a lemon.
entries.definitionCN: 青柠，比柠檬更小更尖。

entries.definition: The sweet citrus, sharing the same trade history.
entries.definitionCN: 甜橙，同样有贸易史。

entries.definition: The large tart citrus of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 同族中较大较酸的柚类。

entries.definition: Slang for something that fails, matching the defective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 俚语「失败品」，对应次品义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real borrowings and the slang sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实借词链与俚语义。

normal.en: The trail runs Persian limun, Arabic laymun, Medieval Latin limon, Old French lemon.
normal.cn: 词路：波斯语 limun → 阿拉伯语 laymun → 中世纪拉丁语 limon → 古法语 lemon。

normal.en: Family: lemony, lemonade.
normal.cn: 词族：lemony、lemonade。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: lemon juice, lemon tree, lemon yellow.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：柠檬汁、柠檬树、柠檬黄。

normal.en: American slang calls a bad car a lemon.
normal.cn: 美国俚语把问题车叫作 lemon。

normal.en: When life gives you lemons is a proverb about turning trouble into good.
normal.cn: 「生活给你柠檬」是化苦为甜的谚语。

abstract.en: Picture your face puckering after one tiny sip.
abstract.cn: 想象小小一口之后整张脸皱起来。

abstract.en: Picture a shiny car that sputters the day after you buy it.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆光鲜的车，买回第二天就熄火。

abstract.en: Picture sour fruit squeezed into sweet tea, trouble turned useful.
abstract.cn: 想象酸果挤进甜茶，麻烦变得有用。

examples.en: Add a slice of lemon to the water and it tastes fresher.
examples.cn: 水里加一片柠檬，喝起来更清新。

examples.en: The market sells lemons from the south in winter.
examples.cn: 市场冬天卖南方来的柠檬。

examples.en: He complained that the laptop he bought was a lemon.
examples.cn: 他抱怨买来的笔记本是台次品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「柠檬」——直接音译，黄皮酸果即柠檬

root: 一般认为经阿拉伯语 laymun 追溯至波斯语 limun，再经中世纪拉丁语 limon 与古法语 lemon 进入英语；具体波斯语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses move from the fruit itself to its tree, taste, colour, drinks, and finally to sour deals and people.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从果实本身走向树、味、色、饮品，最后落到酸涩的交易与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sour yellow fruit that puckers your mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸得让人皱嘴的黄果。

branches.en: THE PLANT: fruit and the tree that bears it.
branches.cn: 植物：果实与结果之树。

branches.en: TASTE AND TASTE PRODUCTS: flavour, colour, and lemon drinks.
branches.cn: 味与味的产品：风味、颜色与柠檬饮。

branches.en: SOUR TRANSFER: sourness spread to bad products and silly people.
branches.cn: 酸的转移：酸味扩散到次品与傻人。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: every sense keeps the sharp yellow profile.
branches.cn: 轴心：每个义项都保留黄而酸的轮廓。

branches.en: NAMED BY SOURCE: colour takes the fruit\u2019s name.
branches.cn: 以源命名：颜色借果名。

intro.en: Lemon is a borrowed noun with no English affixes of its own; derivatives attach English suffixes to it.
intro.cn: lemon 是无英语词缀的外来名词；派生词是在其上附加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native suffix work on a loanword.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示外来词上的本族后缀加工。

items.example: The word followed the fruit trade.

items.exampleCN: 它把 lemon 变成 lemony。

items.example: A lemony smell filled the kitchen.

definition_zh: 借出；借给；增添（色彩等）
definition_en: to give something to someone for a short time, expecting it back; to add a quality to something
core_image: 手伸出去，东西暂时离开你的手
scene: 同学忘了带笔，他从笔袋里抽出一支递过去。Can you lend me your umbrella for an hour?
sceneCN: 这里 lend 是「暂时给出、期待归还」（第 1 个义项：借出）；句意为能否把伞借我一小时。

derivatives.zh: lend 加施事后缀 -er，指「出借人；放贷者」
与 lend 同族（斯堪的纳维亚词源），指「贷款；借出物」

senses.title: To give temporarily, expecting return
senses.definition: to give something to someone for a time, expecting it back
senses.definitionCN: 把某物给某人一段时间，期待归还
senses.example: Can you lend me your umbrella for an hour?
senses.exampleCN: 能把伞借我一小时吗？
senses.why: The core image is a hand stretched out with a return ticket attached.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只伸出去的手，附带着归还的凭据。

senses.title: To provide money at interest
senses.definition: to give money to someone who will pay it back, often with interest
senses.definitionCN: 把钱给将偿还的人，常收利息
senses.example: The bank lends to small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 银行向小企业放贷。
senses.why: Money is just the returnable thing, so lending cash is the same motion with interest attached.
senses.whyCN: 钱不过是可归还之物，放贷就是同一动作附加利息。

senses.title: To add a quality
senses.definition: to give a quality or impression to something
senses.definitionCN: 给某物增添一种品质或印象
senses.example: The sunset lent warmth to the street.
senses.exampleCN: 落日给街道添了暖意。
senses.why: Qualities can be handed over like objects, so the concrete verb stretches to the abstract.
senses.whyCN: 品质可以像物件一样「递」，于是具体动词延伸到抽象。

senses.title: To offer help or attention
senses.definition: to offer a hand, an ear, or support
senses.definitionCN: 提供援手、倾听或支持
senses.example: He lent a hand with the boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 他帮忙搬了箱子。
senses.why: A hand or an ear is lent out and taken back, matching the temporary-giving idea.
senses.whyCN: 援手与耳朵也能「借出归还」，与暂时给出之意吻合。

senses.title: To contribute a role or suitability
senses.definition: to make something suitable for a purpose, as in lend itself to
senses.definitionCN: 使某物适合某用途，如 lend itself to
senses.example: The room lends itself to quiet study.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子适合安静学习。
senses.why: The room hands its features to the activity, as if offering itself on loan.
senses.whyCN: 屋子把自身特质「递」给活动，仿佛把自己出借。

intro.en: Lend comes from Old English laenan "to lend", from Germanic laihiwnjan, related to a root meaning "to let, permit"; loan is a Norse cousin of the same family.
intro.cn: lend 来自古英语 laenan「借出」，出自日耳曼语 laihiwnjan，与意为「允许」的词根相关；loan 是同族的诺斯表亲。

items.en: Old English laenan meant 'to lend', built on a verb meaning 'to let someone have'.
items.cn: 古英语 laenan 意为「借出」，建立在「让某人拥有」的动词之上。

items.en: Germanic laihiwnjan shows the -jan causative ending: to cause someone to have something.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 laihiwnjan 带使役后缀 -jan：使某人拥有某物。

items.en: Norse loan and related laan reinforced the family; English took loan from Norse while keeping lend native.
items.cn: 诺斯语的 loan 及相关形式巩固了词族；英语从诺斯语取 loan，而保留本族的 lend。

items.en: In Middle English lend spread to money-lending as commerce grew.
items.cn: 中古英语随商业发展把 lend 扩展到资金借贷。

items.en: Modern English added the abstract sense of lending qualities, hands and ears.
items.cn: 现代英语新增了借出品质、援手与耳朵的抽象义。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists the give-and-take family.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出给取词族。

entries.definition: Earth as opposed to sea; one vowel apart, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 陆地；仅差一个元音，词根无关。

entries.definition: The past tense of lend; also the church season with capital L.
entries.definitionCN: lend 的过去式；大写 L 也是教会节期。

entries.definition: One who lends, especially money.
entries.definitionCN: 出借者，尤指放贷者。

entries.definition: The noun for the thing lent, or the act; American English also uses loan as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 借出物或行为的名词；美式英语也用 loan 作动词。

entries.definition: To take temporarily; lend is the giving side of the same exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时取用；lend 是同一交换中给出的一侧。

entries.definition: To hand over permanently; lend expects the thing back.
entries.definitionCN: 永久交出；lend 期待归还。

entries.definition: To give formally, often rights or money.
entries.definitionCN: 正式给予，多为权利或资金。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the native root, the family and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用本族词根、词族与习语。

normal.en: Old English laenan meant lend; loan came later from Norse.
normal.cn: 古英语 laenan 意为借出；loan 是后来从诺斯语来的。

normal.en: The pair: borrow in, lend out.
normal.cn: 一对：borrow 进，lend 出。

normal.en: Idioms: lend a hand, lend an ear, lend itself to.
normal.cn: 习语：帮一把、倾听、适合于。

normal.en: Past forms: lends, lent, lending, all regular but with short vowel.
normal.cn: 词形：lends、lent、lending，规则但短元音。

normal.en: Banks lend money; sunsets lend warmth.
normal.cn: 银行放贷；落日增添暖意。

abstract.en: Picture a book leaving your shelf with a promise taped on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书带着归还承诺离开书架。

abstract.en: Picture a golden hour pouring warm light over a grey street.
abstract.cn: 想象金色时刻把暖光泼在灰街道上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing a ball that must come back.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手传递一个必须回来的球。

examples.en: She lent her notes to everyone before the exam.
examples.cn: 考前她把笔记借给了每个人。

examples.en: Please lend me ten minutes of your time.
examples.cn: 请借我十分钟。

examples.en: The old walls lend the town a quiet dignity.
examples.cn: 老墙给小镇添了安静的庄重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「借的」——借的东西总得还 → 借出

root: 古英语 laenan「借出」，出自日耳曼语 laihiwnjan，与「允许」义词根相关；loan 为诺斯语同族借入。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses keep one gesture: something valuable passes out of your hand for a while — objects, money, qualities, or help.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项保持同一手势：贵重之物暂时离开你的手——物件、钱、品质或帮助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand offering something that must come back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手，交出终须归还之物。

branches.en: THINGS AND MONEY: the returnable objects leave your hand.
branches.cn: 物与钱：可归还之物离开你的手。

branches.en: ABSTRACT LOAN: warmth, colour and dignity are also lent.
branches.cn: 抽象之借：暖意、色彩与庄重也可出借。

branches.en: HELP ON LOAN: a hand and an ear are offered and taken back.
branches.cn: 出借的帮助：援手与耳朵可借可还。

branches.en: FITTING ITSELF: the thing offers its own qualities to a purpose.
branches.cn: 自我出借：事物把自身特质供给某一用途。

branches.en: THE RETURN TICKET: every lending expects a coming back.
branches.cn: 归还凭据：每次出借都期待归来。

intro.en: Lend is a short native verb with no prefixes; its family adds agent and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: lend 是无前缀的短小本族动词；词族添加施事与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native suffix work.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族后缀加工。

items.example: The verb is native to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语本族的。
它把 lend 变成 lender。

items.example: The root shows the causative sense.
The idiom keeps the loan idea.
He lent a hand at once.
The hall lends itself to concerts.

definition_zh: 更少的；较少的；减去；不及
definition_en: a smaller amount or degree; to a smaller extent; minus a quantity
core_image: 同样一只杯子，水面比上次低了一截
scene: 期末比期中少睡了许多，他的黑眼圈更深了。This year we have less snow than last year.
sceneCN: 这里 less 是「量或程度的较小」（第 1 个义项：更少的）；句意为今年雪比去年少。

derivatives.zh: less 加后缀 -er，指「较小的；次要的」
less 的最高级，指「最小的；最少的」
less 加动词后缀 -en，指「减少；削弱」

senses.title: A smaller amount
senses.definition: a smaller amount or degree of something
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上更小的
senses.example: This year we have less snow than last year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年雪比去年少。
senses.why: Little steps down to less: the same smallness, now compared.
senses.whyCN: little 的比较级就是 less：同一种「小」，只是加上了比较。

senses.title: To a smaller extent
senses.definition: to a smaller degree; not so much
senses.definitionCN: 程度上较小；没那么……
senses.example: The second film was less exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 第二部电影没那么刺激。
senses.why: Degree shrinks the same way amount does, so the adverb follows the determiner.
senses.whyCN: 程度与数量同样收缩，副词于是跟随限定词。

senses.title: Minus a quantity
senses.definition: after taking away a stated amount
senses.definitionCN: 扣除一定数额之后
senses.example: Nine hundred dollars less tax.
senses.exampleCN: 九百美元扣税后。
senses.why: Taking away shrinks the pile, matching the image of a smaller amount.
senses.whyCN: 扣除使总量变小，与「更少」意象吻合。

senses.title: Not as important or worthy
senses.definition: used to say something is lower in rank or importance
senses.definitionCN: 表示级别或重要性更低
senses.example: Try not to think of it as a lesser task.
senses.exampleCN: 尽量别把它当作次要任务。
senses.why: Being smaller in amount becomes being smaller in worth.
senses.whyCN: 数量之小延伸为价值之低。

senses.title: Even less or none at all
senses.definition: used to intensify a negative, as in still less
senses.definitionCN: 加强否定，如 still less
senses.example: He hardly reads, still less writes.
senses.exampleCN: 他几乎不读书，更别提写作了。
senses.why: If the small thing fails, the smaller one fails more, so less sharpens the negative.
senses.whyCN: 小的尚且不行，更小的更不行，less 因此加强否定。

senses.title: No less — surprisingly much
senses.definition: used to show that an amount is surprisingly large
senses.definitionCN: 表示数量大得出人意料
senses.example: No less than fifty students joined.
senses.exampleCN: 多达五十名学生参加。
senses.why: Doubling the negative form flips the feeling: less phrases can mean much.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式反转出情感：less 的短语也能表示「多」。

intro.en: Less is the comparative of little, from Old English laes, of Germanic origin; its exact root beyond Germanic is uncertain.
intro.cn: less 是 little 的比较级，来自古英语 laes，属日耳曼语源；日耳曼语之外的词根不确定。

items.en: Old English laes was the comparative of lyt 'little', meaning 'smaller, fewer'.
items.cn: 古英语 laes 是 lyt「小」的比较级，意为「更小、更少」。

items.en: Germanic *laisizan underlies the form; related little kept a diminutive ending.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 *laisizan 是其基础；little 则保留了指小词尾。

items.en: Middle English spread less to abstract degree and arithmetic subtraction.
items.cn: 中古英语把 less 扩展到抽象程度与算术减法。

items.en: Modern English fixed less for uncountable amounts, in contrast to fewer.
items.cn: 现代英语固定 less 用于不可数量，与 fewer 相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Germanic trail of the little-family is not agreed on.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：little 词族在日耳曼语之前的轨迹尚无定论。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects the amount-comparing family.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集比较数量的词族。

entries.definition: A class or task; shares five letters but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 课程；共享五个字母，词根不同。

entries.definition: The adjective form of less for rank and importance.
entries.definitionCN: less 的形容词形式，指级别与重要性。

entries.definition: The superlative of little and less.
entries.definitionCN: little 与 less 的最高级。

entries.definition: For countable things; less is for amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 用于可数；less 用于不可数量。

entries.definition: The arithmetic word for taking away.
entries.definitionCN: 算术中的「减去」。

entries.definition: Smaller in degree or position.
entries.definitionCN: 程度或位置更低。

entries.definition: The base adjective; less is its comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 原级形容词；less 是其比较级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the little-family and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 little 词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Less is the comparative of little; least is the superlative.
normal.cn: less 是 little 的比较级；least 是最高级。

normal.en: Use less for amounts, fewer for counts: less water, fewer bottles.
normal.cn: 量用 less，可数用 fewer：less water、fewer bottles。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: no less than, more or less, none the less.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：多达、或多或少、尽管如此。

normal.en: Lessen is the verb: to make less.
normal.cn: lessen 是动词：使更少。

normal.en: Nine dollars less tax means after tax is taken away.
normal.cn: nine dollars less tax 指扣税之后。

abstract.en: Picture one glass with a visibly lower water line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子水位明显更低。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt where tax is sliced off the total.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上税额从总额里被切掉。

abstract.en: Picture a shrinking row of books, one less each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书逐周减少，一本更比一本少。

examples.en: There is less traffic on Sundays.
examples.cn: 周日路上车少。

examples.en: The trip took two hours less than we expected.
examples.cn: 旅程比预期少花两小时。

examples.en: She earns less but enjoys the work more.
examples.cn: 她挣得更少，却更喜欢这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累死」——钱越挣越少，累死了 → 更少

root: 古英语 laes「较小」，日耳曼语源，是 little 的比较级；更早词根不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses compare downward: smaller amounts, smaller degrees, subtraction, lower worth, sharpened negatives, and a flipped phrase meaning much.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项一路向下比：更小的量、更低的程度、减法、更低的价值、强化的否定，以及反转出「多达」的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the water line drops; the same container holds less.
core.cn: 核心意象：水位下降，同一容器装得更少。

branches.en: SMALLER EVERYWHERE: amounts and degrees shrink together.
branches.cn: 处处变小：数量与程度一同收缩。

branches.en: TAKING AWAY: subtraction is less written as arithmetic.
branches.cn: 减去：减法就是 less 的算术形态。

branches.en: SMALL IN WORTH: little amount becomes low rank.
branches.cn: 价值之小：数量小变成级别低。

branches.en: SHARPENED NEGATIVES: still less pushes denial further.
branches.cn: 强化否定：still less 把否定推得更远。

branches.en: THE FLIP SIDE: no less than surprisingly means much.
branches.cn: 反转面：no less than 出人意料地表示多。

intro.en: Less is a short native comparative with no prefixes; its family is little, least, lesser and lessen.
intro.cn: less 是无前缀的本族比较级；词族为 little、least、lesser、lessen。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show the native family.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族词族。

items.example: A lesser poet still wrote well.

items.exampleCN: 它把 less 变成 lessen。

items.example: The work is more or less done.

definition_zh: 课；课程；教训；一堂课的时间
definition_en: a period of teaching; a piece of content studied; an experience that teaches you something
core_image: 黑板前的一段时间，离开时你比来时知道得多
scene: 雨天的午后，音乐教室里传来断续的琴声。The first lesson begins at eight sharp.
sceneCN: 这里 lesson 是「教学时段」（第 1 个义项：一节课）；句意为第一节课八点整开始。

pos.zh: 课程内容；功课外的东西

derivatives.zh: lesson 加 -ing 名词化，指「授课过程」（罕用）
加否定前缀 un-，指「未受过教的」（罕用）

senses.title: A period of teaching
senses.definition: a set period in which someone is taught
senses.definitionCN: 安排好的教学时段
senses.example: The first lesson begins at eight sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 第一节课八点整开始。
senses.why: The reading is part of lesson: a portion read aloud became a portion taught.
senses.whyCN: 「诵读的部分」是 lesson 的本义：读的一段变成了教的一段。

senses.title: The content studied
senses.definition: the material or subject covered in teaching
senses.definitionCN: 教学中涵盖的材料或科目
senses.example: Today\u2019s lesson is about rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的课讲河流。
senses.why: The period and what fills it share the name, since the lesson is what is delivered.
senses.whyCN: 时段与其中所授共享其名，因为 lesson 就是所授之物。

senses.title: An experience that teaches
senses.definition: something learned from experience, often a hard one
senses.definitionCN: 从经历中学到的东西，常含挫折
senses.example: The accident taught him a lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 那次事故给了他一个教训。
senses.why: Life also delivers portions of instruction, so the classroom word covers the school of hard knocks.
senses.whyCN: 生活也会「授课」，课堂之词于是覆盖了社会这所学校。

senses.title: A passage from scripture
senses.definition: a passage read aloud in church services
senses.definitionCN: 礼拜中朗读的经文段落
senses.example: The second lesson comes from the gospel.
senses.exampleCN: 第二段诵读取自福音书。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense kept: the reading portion survives in church use.
senses.whyCN: 这是保存最久的义项：诵读段落留存于教会用法。

senses.title: A warning meant to correct
senses.definition: a punishment or rebuke intended to teach someone better
senses.definitionCN: 意在使人改正的惩罚或训诫
senses.example: The coach gave them a hard lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 教练狠狠敲打了他们一顿。
senses.why: A sharp correction is a lesson in disguise, delivered without a classroom.
senses.whyCN: 严厉的纠正是伪装的课，只是不在教室里上。

senses.title: A unit in a course or book
senses.definition: a numbered unit of a course or textbook
senses.definitionCN: 课程或教材中编号的一单元
senses.example: Unit five has ten lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 第五单元有十课。
senses.why: Books slice teaching into portions, each portion keeping the old word.
senses.whyCN: 书籍把教学切成段落，每段沿用旧词。

intro.en: Lesson comes from Old French lecon, from Medieval Latin lecio, from Latin lectio "a reading", built on legere "to read, gather".
intro.cn: lesson 来自古法语 lecon，出自中世纪拉丁语 lecio，再溯至拉丁语 lectio「诵读」，建立在 legere「读、采集」之上。

items.en: Latin legere meant 'to gather, read', the same root as legible and lectern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为「采集、读」，与 legible、lectern 同根。

items.en: Latin lectio meant 'a reading', especially a passage read aloud, as in church.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lectio 意为「诵读」，尤指朗读的段落，见于教会。

items.en: Medieval Latin lecio shifted to mean a piece of teaching itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 lecio 转指教学本身的一部分。

items.en: Old French lecon carried the teaching sense into English spelling and sound.
items.cn: 古法语 lecon 把教学义带入英语的拼写与读音。

items.en: Modern English spread lesson to classes, books, punishments and the school of experience.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lesson 扩展到课堂、教材、惩戒与经验之校。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects teaching words.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集教学之词。

entries.definition: The verb to reduce; identical in sound, unrelated in root.
entries.definitionCN: 减少的动词；同音但词根无关。

entries.definition: The comparative amount word; shares letters only.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级「更少」；只是字母相叠。

entries.definition: From the same Latin legere family; a long talk of teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 legere 词族；指较长的授课演讲。

entries.definition: The group or session; lesson stresses the content taught.
entries.definitionCN: 班级或课时；lesson 强调所授内容。

entries.definition: Teaching, often step by step; more formal than lesson.
entries.definitionCN: 教学，多为分步；比 lesson 正式。

entries.definition: The lesson drawn from a story, especially a fable.
entries.definitionCN: 从故事中得出的寓意，尤指寓言。

entries.definition: A period of activity or study; broader than a lesson.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或学习的一段；比 lesson 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin root and real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁词根与真实短语。

normal.en: Latin lectio meant a reading; a lesson began as a read portion.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lectio 意为诵读；lesson 起初就是读的一段。

normal.en: The same root gives lecture, legible and lectern.
normal.cn: 同根词有 lecture、legible、lectern。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: give a lesson, learn a lesson, teach someone a lesson.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：授课、吸取教训、教训某人。

normal.en: Churches still call scripture readings the lessons.
normal.cn: 教会至今把诵读经文叫 lessons。

normal.en: A lesson plan is the teacher\u2019s map for one class.
normal.cn: 教案是教师一节课的路线图。

abstract.en: Picture a bell, and forty heads bending over one page.
abstract.cn: 想象铃声响后，四十个脑袋凑向同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a bruise that remembers the warning better than words.
abstract.cn: 想象一块淤青比言语更牢地记住警告。

abstract.en: Picture a pulpit light on one open scripture page.
abstract.cn: 想象讲坛灯光落在一页摊开的经文上。

examples.en: Piano lessons cost twice as much this year.
examples.cn: 今年钢琴课涨了一倍。

examples.en: Every failure carries a lesson if you look for it.
examples.cn: 只要去找，每次失败都藏着一课。

examples.en: The vicar read the first lesson from Isaiah.
examples.cn: 牧师领读了取自以赛亚书的第一段经文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「雷声」——老师讲课时如雷贯耳 → 课；教训

root: 拉丁语 lectio「诵读」（legere「读、采集」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 lecio → 古法语 lecon → 英语 lesson；与 lecture 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all keep the shape of a portion delivered: a reading, a class, its content, a unit, a warning, and a hard-won truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都保留「被交付的一段」的形状：诵读、课、内容、单元、警告与苦得的道理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measured portion of teaching, handed over like a read passage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段有定量的教学，如诵读般交付。

branches.en: MEASURED TIME: the class period and the book unit.
branches.cn: 定量时间：课堂时段与教材单元。

branches.en: WHAT IS DELIVERED: the content inside the period.
branches.cn: 所授之物：时段里的内容。

branches.en: THE OLDEST SENSE: scripture readings survive in church.
branches.cn: 最老义项：教会里存活的经文诵读。

branches.en: THE HARD SCHOOL: experience and punishment both teach.
branches.cn: 严苛学校：经验与惩戒皆可施教。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: every sense is a portion handed over.
branches.cn: 轴心：每个义项都是交付的一段。

intro.en: Lesson is a borrowed noun with no English affixes of its own; derivatives are rare and attach native prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: lesson 是无本族词缀的外来名词；派生词少见，附加本族前后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root legere gives cousins like lecture, so the Latin section lists them; no direct Latin cognate of lesson itself is listed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 legere 提供 lecture 等同族词，拉丁部分列出它们；lesson 本体的直接拉丁同源词不另列。
